what: 004's M10 thread run from the free top end, vanishing over a 3 mm (2 P) runout before the d16 shoulder
method: the shaft's lower end is a shoulder (the d16 collar lies past it, in the groove's way), so the groove (its runout included) stops with its widest part clear of it: its centre w = (P/4 + 2 (d/2 + 0.05P - r_root) tan30)/2 = 0.699551 mm above the shoulder (its half width at the tool's outer edge, 0.05 P past the crest), and the square stop inside material removes exactly as if the groove ended at its centre (see 003); the top end is free, the groove runs out into the air. The runout (ease_out, at the end away from `from`) moves the groove's section out of the shaft as it turns, linearly from h = d/2 - root + 0.05P at s = 10 + w to 0 at s + 3: the cut per radian is f(o) = int r w(r - o) dr from root + o to 5 (w the section's width at its own radius), the runout removes 2 pi (3/P) mean(f) (Simpson, exact on the cubic), the full-depth groove from s + 3 to the free top end 2 pi f(0) (35 - s - 3)/P (the overrun past the free end as in 001). V = pi 8^2 10 + pi 5^2 25 - both. Tolerance 0.01%: SMLib's exact radial screw sweep
